note:
⛔ SNG-441. FOOTHILLS AND FOLK — Erik, 2026-08-15: 'Foothills are the FUNCTIONAL VERSION of the pole in many cases; in some cases the place that is APPROACHABLE and the ECONOMIC CENTER. They are also NOT strictly one pole per parent. We need balance, but foothills are most likely a BLEND of a primary domain with 1-2 of its neighbors.'
⚠️ THERE ARE 26 CANONICAL TRADITIONS — 24 ring poles on 12 axes, plus god_named and bargainers already carrying `pole: foothill`. I had been counting 31 by treating collection-keys as peoples.
_theRule:
⛔ A FOOTHILL IS NOT A LESSER TRADITION — IT IS A POLE MADE USABLE. The pole states the position absolutely; the foothill is what you can actually buy, hire, learn and live beside. ⚠️ AND THE EXISTING TWO PROVE THE BLEND CROSSES AXES rather than staying on neighbours:
   GOD-NAMED — 'borrowed grandeur worn slightly wrong; a man addressed by a name nobody in this valley can check.' ⛔ THAT IS SERAPHIC (angelic authority) BLENDED WITH VEILWRIGHT (falsehood). The functional version of divine authority is a borrowed one.
   BARGAINERS — 'a good table, a fair scale, an exit that is always shown to you and always costed.' ⛔ ABYSSAL (the named want, the struck term) BLENDED WITH VERIST (truth). The functional version of the bargain is an HONEST one, which is precisely why anyone sits down twice.
⚠️ SO THE PATTERN IS: TAKE THE POLE'S POWER AND ADD WHAT MAKES IT SURVIVABLE TO DEAL WITH.
⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15, REFINEMENT: 'It's likely that these foothills will have THREE DOMAINS, as each character does.' ⚠️ THAT IS THE RULE — a foothill is not a pole plus a qualifier, it is a THREE-DOMAIN BLEND, the same shape a player character has. Which is the point: a foothill is where the world is LIVED IN rather than argued from.
⛔ HARDLINE IS THE CLEANEST EXAMPLE OF THE PATTERN: pole + neighbour (method) + ANTIPODE (the thing that makes it sellable). god_named blends authority with falsehood, bargainers blends appetite with truth, hardline blends violence with peace. ⚠️ IN EVERY CASE THE SECOND OR THIRD DOMAIN IS WHAT LETS OTHER PEOPLE DEAL WITH THE FIRST.
⛔ GREYHEARTH ADDS A CASE: A FOOTHILL MAY ALREADY EXIST AS A PLACE BEFORE IT IS AUTHORED AS A TRADITION. ⚠️ Check the location seeds before authoring a foothill — `greyhearth` had its blend, its economy and its ethic written into its own description and was not in this file.

god_named.status: ⚠️ weights revised — seraphic raised to 0.6 now that Erik has ruled this a fidelity relation rather than a blend of equals.
god_named._thirdDomain: ⚠️ Proposed under the three-domain rule: LATTICE for the hall, the office and the retinue — borrowed grandeur needs an administration to be borrowed FROM.
god_named._seraphicRelation:
⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15: 'The Seraphs are SIMILAR TO the God-named — although many of them have managed to hold to the IDEALS of the angels, and the most legendary ones are ARCHANGELS. The God-named are the more human, FALLIBLE ones, yet still have similar powers. There are also FALLEN Seraphs.'
⚠️ SO THIS IS NOT A POWER DIFFERENCE — IT IS A FIDELITY DIFFERENCE, and it is the sharpest foothill relation on the wheel. Same ordered-nanite apparatus, three standings:
   ARCHANGEL — a Seraph who held the ideal. Legendary tier, and rare by definition.
   SERAPH — holds it imperfectly, and knows it.
   GOD-NAMED — ⛔ HUMAN AND FALLIBLE, WITH THE SAME POWERS. 'Borrowed grandeur worn slightly wrong; a man addressed by a name nobody in this valley can check.' The foothill is not weaker — it is HONEST ABOUT BEING WORN BY A PERSON.
   FALLEN SERAPH — ⛔ THE FOURTH STATE, AND THE ONE WITH STORY IN IT. Held the ideal, lost it, and kept the apparatus. ⚠️ A fallen Seraph is not a demon: the Abyssals draw on PRECURSOR and the Seraphim on ORDERED NANITE, so falling does not change your source. It changes what you are running the machinery FOR, which is worse.
god_named._parentsBasis: ⬜ NOT RE-DERIVED — only 3 craft(s) carry `learnedAt: god_named`. ⚠️ Three data points cannot correct a three-way blend; the measured split would just BE the three crafts. Authored values stand until the place has enough craft to speak for itself.

bargainers.status: authored — blend inferred from aesthetic, ⚠️ Erik to confirm the weights
bargainers._thirdDomain: ⚠️ Proposed: MASON for the fair scale and the honest weight — 'only what can be touched is real' is the Bargainers' guarantee as much as the Masons'.
bargainers._parentsBasis: ⬜ NOT RE-DERIVED — only 3 craft(s) carry `learnedAt: bargainers`. ⚠️ Three data points cannot correct a three-way blend; the measured split would just BE the three crafts. Authored values stand until the place has enough craft to speak for itself.

harmonic.ratified: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15: 'I agree with you about the Threnodists with the lattice aesthetic for the resonant/harmonic foothill.'
harmonic.why: ⚠️ THRENODIST FOR CRAFT, LATTICE FOR AESTHETIC — the Threnodists sing what they FEEL; the Heights sing what they can BUILD WITH. Sound made structural: standing waves, phononic crystal, interference held as architecture. ⛔ AND LATTICE IS NOT A THRENODIST RING-NEIGHBOUR (pos 15 vs 23), which is fine — the two existing foothills also blend across the ring.
harmonic.note: ⚠️ Sound is not one of the twelve axes. The foothill is where it enters the world.
harmonic._thirdDomain: ⚠️ THIRD DOMAIN ADDED under Erik's three-domain rule. MASON, and the seed argues it: 'buildings GROWN FROM PHONONIC CRYSTAL hum at frequencies you feel in your teeth', and the terraces are cut. ⛔ THRENODIST GIVES SOUND, LATTICE GIVES STRUCTURE, MASON GIVES THE MATERIAL — you cannot hold a standing wave in air alone; something has to be shaped to ring. ⚠️ Erik to confirm mason over numinous, which would make it meaning-in-sound instead.
harmonic._parentsRederived_20260902: ⚠️ THE BLEND WAS A GUESS AND THE CRAFTS DISAGREED. Authored 2026-08-15 as threnodist .5 / lattice .3 / mason .2, BEFORE any craft carried a lineage. The 16 crafts assigned under R33 measure mason 6 · lattice 5 · threnodist 5 — the SMALLEST authored parent taking the MOST crafts. ⛔ Sound-work at the Heights turns out to be more MATERIAL than mournful: `shatterpoint` finds where matter breaks, `chord_of_mending` sings a thing's GRAIN, `sonic_resonance` shatters at a distance, `tremor_sense` reads the ground. ✅ Pathos still holds a third — `worldsong`, `echo_memory`, `harmonic_voice` — but it does not lead. ➡️ Re-derived from the crafts, which are better evidence of who lives there than a guess made before they existed.
harmonic._parentsBasis: ⚑ re-derived from 16 crafts carrying `learnedAt: harmonic` after the R33 lineage assignment.

radiant_folk.ratified: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15: 'Radiant plateau can be light, wright, and order.'
radiant_folk.why:
⛔ LIGHT + MAKING + ORDER, and the crafts show all three. BLAZEBORN gives the medium — Radiance is theirs. WRIGHT gives the turn that makes it usable: Light Well STORES light, Clarity Lens SHAPES it, Beacon Thread STRINGS it between people. LATTICE gives the discipline — light-guides paved into streets and towers that braid sunlight into working beams are an infrastructure, laid out and maintained.
⚠️ THE DIFFERENCE FROM THE PARENT, PLAINLY: A BLAZEBORN SPENDS LIGHT TO EXPOSE SOMETHING AND THE LIGHT IS GONE. THE PLATEAU STORES IT AND SELLS IT. ⛔ That is what makes a foothill an economic centre — the pole performs its position, the foothill runs a utility.
radiant_folk._parentsRederived_20260902: ✅ THE GUESS WAS NEARLY RIGHT. Authored blazeborn .5 / wright .3 / lattice .2; the 15 crafts measure blazeborn 8 (.53) · wright 5 (.33) · lattice 2 (.13). ⚠️ Only Makecraft and Latticework swap a little weight — the Plateau makes MORE objects and imposes LESS order than the guess allowed: `glasswork`, `light_well`, `clarity_lens`, `glimmer_script`, `sun_seal` are all made things.
radiant_folk._parentsBasis: ⚑ re-derived from 15 crafts carrying `learnedAt: radiant_folk` after the R33 lineage assignment.

hardline.ratified: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15: 'The Marchers foothill likely produces fantastic martial training, as well as mercenary units.'
hardline.why:
⛔ THE BLEND IS ALREADY IN HARDLINE'S OWN SEED, which I authored without seeing what it was: 'drill-yards, body-halls and mediators in one town, DELIBERATELY. The only place where a marcher and a stillholder train in the same yard, and it works because everyone here has needed both.'
   MARCHER gives the Edge — force made exact, the line that holds.
   SOMATIC gives the teaching. ⚠️ A ring-neighbour (pos 6 and 7), and the reason this foothill can TRAIN rather than merely fight: the Marchers have discipline, the Somatics have a method for putting a body through it. Body-halls beside drill-yards.
   STILLHOLD gives the contract. ⛔ MARCHER'S OWN ANTIPODE, and that is not a contradiction — it is what makes the violence SELLABLE. A company that will stop when the terms say stop can be hired by someone who has to live in the town afterwards.
hardline.theFunctionalTurn: ⛔ THE POLE HOLDS A LINE OUT OF CONVICTION. THE FOOTHILL HOLDS ONE UNDER CONTRACT. ⚠️ That is the whole difference and it is not a diminishment — a conviction cannot be hired, budgeted for, or relieved at the end of a season. The March exists because someone visibly will not move; Hardline exists because someone will move, on the date agreed, for the agreed fee, and both parties know it in advance.

produces.detail: ⛔ THE BEST IN THE WORLD, and available to anyone who pays — which the Marchers find distasteful and use anyway. A season at Hardline is how a valley guard-captain becomes worth the title.

⚠️ Raised, drilled, contracted and DISBANDED here. The disbanding is the part that matters — a company that cannot be dissolved is not a company, it is an occupation, and Hardline's whole standing rests on never having produced one.
⛔ The stillholder share, working. Duels, trials-by-arms and settlements fought under a mediator who can stop it. ⚠️ People bring their wars here to have them fought SMALLER.
The body-halls. What real use does to a person, addressed by people who have seen it before — and the reason the queue at the Grindstone exists at all.

hardline._abilityGap:
⛔ RESOLVED BY THE TWO-AXIS RULE RATHER THAN BY MOVING CRAFTS INTO IT. Hardline has zero abilities OF ITS OWN and should — it is a place of ACCESS. Five of the six new physical crafts now list it under `learnedAt` while rooting to marcher, somatic or valley_craft.
⚠️ WHETHER A FOOTHILL SHOULD EVER HAVE ITS OWN ROOTED CRAFTS IS STILL ERIK'S CALL — harmonic and radiant_folk between them hold 29, so the precedent says yes. ⛔ THE DISTINCTION I WOULD DRAW: a foothill roots a craft when the BLEND produces something neither parent has. Glasswork is not Radiance done cheaply; it is light stored and sold, which no Blazeborn would author. Hardline's equivalent would be a craft about CONTRACTED violence — starting, stopping and being paid — that neither the Marchers nor the Stillhold would ever write down.
hardline._parentsBasis: ⬜ NOT RE-DERIVED — only 1 craft(s) carry `learnedAt: hardline`. ⚠️ Three data points cannot correct a three-way blend; the measured split would just BE the three crafts. Authored values stand until the place has enough craft to speak for itself.

greyhearth.ratified: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-16: 'If we don't have a Foothill for the GRAVE-CALLERS, ASHWARDENS, NECROMANCERS and their adjacents, then yes there needs to be a Foothill.'
greyhearth.why:
⚠️ IT ALREADY EXISTED AND WAS ALREADY THE RIGHT PLACE. `greyhearth` is authored as 'the burying trades, the mourning trades AND THE QUIET ONES — a town that buries for every road that meets here, the Crossing's dead and the Palelands' both, and does not find it grim: everyone here has handled it.' ⛔ IT ALREADY BLENDS BOTH SECTS IN ITS OWN SEED.
   ASHWARDEN gives the craft — ending, tending, and what remains addressable.
   THRENODIST gives the mourning trades. ⚠️ A burial town that could not hold a funeral would be a disposal site.
   WRIGHT gives the third domain: ⛔ COFFINS, CAIRNS, MARKERS, BARROWS AND THE MACHINERY OF A CEMETERY. Someone makes those, and at scale.
greyhearth.theFunctionalTurn: ⛔ THE POLE TENDS AN ENDING BECAUSE IT IS OWED. THE FOOTHILL TENDS IT BECAUSE IT WAS PAID FOR — and that is what makes it available to people who are not Ashwardens. ⚠️ Cairnhold will come when your dead are its business. Greyhearth comes when you hire it.

produces.detail: Named in Set Hand and authored nowhere until now. ⚠️ THEY ARE THE FOOTHILL'S NECROMANCERS — set labour, hauling crews, mine-shifts and harvest hands that do not tire. ⛔ THE PALELANDS 'HAVE NEVER PRETENDED OTHERWISE'; Greyhearth invoices for it.
Gravediggers, coffin-wrights, cairn-masons, corpse-carriers, and the people who wash and dress the dead. A trade, with apprentices.
⚠️ Threnodists who sing for people they never met, and do it properly. A town that buries for every road needs mourners who do not run out.
True Account sold as a service — what is failing in a person, a wall or a house, and how long it has. People come here to be told.

greyhearth._erikRules: ⚠️ whether `wright` is the right third domain, or `mason` (cairns and stone) — both are defensible and wright covers the coffin-and-machinery half better
greyhearth._note:
⛔ AND IT ANSWERS THE ADJACENCY ERIK NAMED. Ashwardens, Necromancers, Grave-Callers and 'their adjacents' — the burying trades, the mourning trades, the quiet ones — are one economy, and Greyhearth is where that economy is.
⛔ AND THE TWO BANKS RESOLVE THE THIRD-DOMAIN QUESTION: WRIGHT SERVES BOTH. The grey bank makes coffins and markers; the far bank makes REGALIA, instruments, bone-work and the machinery of procession. ⚠️ Same craft, and the two banks would not agree it was the same craft.

twoBanks._ruling:
⛔ ERIK 2026-08-16: 'I think we might want MORE to Greyhearth. Maybe there are TWO SIDES TO THE FOOTHILL SEPARATED BY A RIVER. One side is the grey and morose one you described, and the other can be MORE MYSTICAL, COLORFUL, AND DANGEROUS — purples and greens and regalia and celebrations, RITUALS, POWER.'
⚠️ AND IT FIXES SOMETHING I HAD MISSED: a foothill is where a pole becomes usable, and I had only written the SAFE half. ⛔ THE ASHWARDEN POLE IS NOT SAFE — it holds The Cut Thread. A burying town that expressed only the tending half would be the pole rounded down.

GREY BANK.name: Greyhearth proper — the near bank
GREY BANK.palette: ⚠️ Grey, bone, undyed wool, wet stone. Nothing is decorated because decoration would be a claim.
GREY BANK.who: Gravediggers, coffin-wrights, cairn-masons, corpse-washers, hired mourners, reckoners.
GREY BANK.ethic: ⛔ EVERYONE HERE HAS HANDLED IT. Death is a trade and trades are unglamorous. You are not frightened of them and they are not impressed by you.
GREY BANK.sells: Burial, mourning, last accounts, a true reckoning of what is failing.
GREY BANK._note: ⚠️ THE LEAST FRIGHTENING PLACE IN THE WORLD, and it is the near bank because it is the one that faces the roads.

twoBanks.theRiver:
⛔ ONE BRIDGE BETWEEN GREYHEARTH AND AMARANTH. Both towns agree something persists after an ending — they differ on what is owed to it. GREYHEARTH TENDS IT AND LETS IT GO. AMARANTH TALKS TO IT.
⚠️ AND IT IS MOSTLY NOT A QUARREL. Some on each side hold it as a real disagreement and will say so, but MOST PEOPLE HERE SIMPLY HAVE A WAY THEY PREFER TO WORK AND KNOW THERE IS A TIME AND A PLACE FOR BOTH. ⛔ A GREYHEARTH RECKONER WILL SEND YOU OVER THE BRIDGE WITHOUT COMMENT WHEN WHAT YOU NEED IS THERE, and an Amaranth caller will tell you to go back down when a burial is all you actually want.
⚠️ The two towns are the tradition's two answers made into geography, and most of their people use both.
_playHooks: ⚠️ A grey-bank funeral and a far-bank procession for the same body, on the same day.
⛔ The bridge is the only crossing and both banks control an end of it.
⚠️ Someone hires the far bank for something the grey bank would have done cheaper and worse.
⛔ The year's dead are carried across and BACK — and one year, something is carried back that was not carried over.
twoBanks._designNote: ⛔ CORRECTED TWICE ON THIS ENTRY. (1) 'The only place in the world where death is a party' — NOT THE ONLY PLACE, and I had no basis for the claim. (2) 'Visitors find it more disturbing than the graves' — VISITORS COME IN MANY TYPES and a blanket reaction is worldbuilding by assertion. ⚠️ Erik: 'don't generalize.' (3) 'The split is an argument' — SOME SEE IT THAT WAY; most just have a preferred way of operating.

AMARANTH.name: ⛔ AMARANTH — the sister town across the river
AMARANTH.palette: ⛔ PURPLE AND DEEP GREEN, gold thread, bone worked into regalia rather than buried. Lamplit, loud, and coloured in a way nothing else in the Palelands is.
AMARANTH.who: ⛔ THE GRAVE-CALLERS, the ritualists, the ones who take the tradition's central claim seriously enough to act on it, and the people who pay them.
AMARANTH.ethic: ⛔ IF SOMETHING PERSISTS AFTER AN ENDING, IT CAN BE ADDRESSED — AND THE HIGH BANK ADDRESSES IT. Not furtively and not in cellars: in procession, in season, with music.
AMARANTH.sells: Set labour by the crew. Answers from the recently dead. Attendance at a death that is going to be difficult. ⛔ AND, RARELY AND EXPENSIVELY, A WALK BACK — Calling Back is not a secret here, it is a price.
AMARANTH.celebrations:
⚠️ RITUALS AND FESTIVALS, and they are celebrations rather than solemnities: the night the names are sung, the setting of the season's crews, the procession where the year's dead are carried across the bridge and BACK.
⚠️ HOW A VISITOR TAKES IT VARIES AND SHOULD BE PLAYED THAT WAY. A Threnodist finds it correct. A Blazeborn finds it obscene. A Lattice factor finds it well-run. ⛔ AND SOME FIND IT RESTRAINED — the Wild Half does louder, and the Abyssals do it with worse manners.
AMARANTH.danger: ⛔ POWER, AND IT IS NOT PRETENDING OTHERWISE. Things are set here that should be asked permission of. Things are asked here that answer. ⚠️ People cross the bridge and come back changed, or come back owing, or do not come back — and the High Bank does not regard any of those as a failure of the service.
AMARANTH._name:
⛔ ERIK: 'I don't want it to be a bank. Maybe GREYHEARTH is the grey bank and its SISTER ACROSS THE RIVER is a different name completely — a more fantasy name.'
⚠️ AMARANTH: from Greek ἀμάραντος, UNFADING — a- (not) + marainein (to wither). ⛔ THE WORD IS THE TOWN'S WHOLE POSITION: it is the flower that does not wilt, it is purple, and ITS ROOT IS THE NEGATION OF `WITHER` — which is an Ashwarden craft by name.
⚠️ AND THE PAIRING WORKS: GREYHEARTH is grey, domestic, a hearth. AMARANTH is purple, ceremonial, and claims that nothing finishes. Two towns, one river, opposite answers, and neither name mentions the other.

_playHooks: ⚠️ A Greyhearth funeral and an Amaranth procession for the same body, on the same day — arranged by the same family without friction.
⛔ The bridge is the only crossing and each town keeps an end of it.
⚠️ Someone hires Amaranth for something Greyhearth would have done cheaper and worse — or slower and better.
⛔ The year's dead are carried over and BACK — and one year, something is carried back that was not carried over.
greyhearth.name: Greyhearth and Amaranth
greyhearth._parentsBasis: ⬜ NOT RE-DERIVED — ZERO crafts authored. ⚠️ The blend is pure design intent (ashwarden .5 / threnodist .3 / wright .2) and stays that way until Greyhearth has crafts.

valley_craft.ratified: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-23: 'valley_craft DO have parents — we've established this multiple times.'
valley_craft.why:
⚠️ I RECORDED IT TWICE AS 'THE FOLK COLLECTION, NO PARENTS' AND WAS CORRECTED BOTH TIMES. ⛔ THE DEFINITION IS THE THING I KEPT MISSING: A FOOTHILL IS WHERE MULTIPLE TRADITIONS COME TOGETHER — A PLACE WHERE A DOMAIN AND ITS ADJACENTS LIVE AND WORK. That is a description of the CROSSING, which is the most foothill-shaped place in the world.
   STILLHOLD 0.4 — the mediator's share. The Crossing holds because someone stops things.
   WRIGHT 0.3 — it is a working valley: made goods, repair, the trades.
   ROOTKIN 0.3 — it is a GROWING valley, and the green is half of what the folk crafts handle.
valley_craft.theFunctionalTurn: ⛔ THE POLES ARE CLOSED AND VALLEY CRAFT IS OPEN. traditions.json: 'the Valley's folk traditions (harmonic/radiant/valley_craft) are OPEN — they are the near-center crossing; anyone in the Valley may learn them.' ⚠️ THAT IS THE FOOTHILL PROPERTY STATED IN THE ACCESS RULES and I read it as evidence it was NOT a foothill.
valley_craft._note: ⛔ AND IT SATISFIES THE ROOTING TEST ALREADY IN THIS FILE: 'a foothill roots a craft when the BLEND produces something neither parent has.' ⚠️ 18 crafts, and they are the crossing's own — not stillhold done cheaply, not wright done small.

_supersededReading._note:
⛔ CCODE-221 · ONE RECORD NOW — AND THIS IS NOT A TIDY-UP, IT IS TWO ERIK STATEMENTS THAT DISAGREE.
⚠️ Aevi's §4 said §44.2 settles it: valley_craft IS a foothill and HAS parents. ⛔ BUT THE BLOCK THIS NOTE ABSORBED OPENS "ERIK AGREED THE ALLOCATION: `valley_craft` is FOLK, not a foothill" — with a definition attached: a FOOTHILL is the functional version of ONE pole and is a tradition; FOLK is the ordinary person's version of MANY, no single parent, no gate, learnable by anyone.
⛔ SO THIS IS THE `seraphic`/`abyssal` SHAPE AGAIN: two rulings, both cited, and a repair that would have quietly picked one. It is preserved VERBATIM below and neither is deleted.
✅ WHAT IS NOT IN DISPUTE, AND WHY THE ENGINE IS UNAFFECTED EITHER WAY: the parents (stillhold .4 / wright .3 / rootkin .3) compute to `metaphysical`, which is exactly what all 18 valley_craft crafts already carry. The label is contested; the SOURCE is not.
⚠️ Its old mix `body 0.75 / precursor 0.20 / nanite 0.05` is built from two names that are no longer sources at all — a superseded reading carrying a superseded vocabulary, which is the clearest evidence of which statement is older.

supersededRecord._ruling:
⛔ ERIK AGREED THE ALLOCATION: `valley_craft` is FOLK, not a foothill. THE DISTINCTION: a FOOTHILL is the functional version of ONE pole, has a place and an economy, and is a tradition. FOLK is the ordinary person's version of MANY — no single parent, no gate, learnable by anyone.
⚠️ Wayfinding, Greenlore, Rivercraft, Quiet Step, Stonewise, Hearthbinding. `body 0.75 / precursor 0.20 / nanite 0.05`, and two are openly borrowed — 'the valley's BORROWED sound-work' (Carrying Call) and Glasswork, 'what a people learn from living under the plateau edge.'

valley_craft._zeroAbilitiesIsCorrect_20260831: ✅ THIS RECORD HAS ZERO ABILITIES AND THAT IS THE RECORD WORKING, NOT AN UNFINISHED RETIREMENT. ⛔ CCode asked (`RULING_REQUEST_ccode_c_and_d` §2): 'either a retirement that has not finished, or AN ACCESS POINT THAT OUTLIVES ITS CRAFTS.' ✅ IT IS THE SECOND, and this record's own `why` field says so: 'A FOOTHILL IS WHERE MULTIPLE TRADITIONS COME TOGETHER — A PLACE.' ⚠️ `place: the_crossing` · `region: the_given_land`. **The crafts moved to their real owners when Erik emptied valley_craft into the poles; THE ACCESS POINT DID NOT MOVE, BECAUSE A PLACE CANNOT.** ✅ AND `hardline` AND `greyhearth` PROVE THE SHAPE: both have zero abilities and always have, and nobody has called them unfinished. ⛔ What this record now says is: **the Crossing is where stillhold, wright and rootkin meet, and what is practised there is open to anyone.**
valley_craft._parentsRederived_20260902: ⛔ THE BIGGEST CORRECTION, AND IT CONFIRMS WHAT VALLEY CRAFT IS. Authored as a three-way stillhold .4 / wright .3 / rootkin .3. The 15 crafts measure TEN parents: mason 3 · horizon 2 · rootkin 2 · stillhold 2 · then wright, umbral, threnodist, lattice, veilwright, marcher at one each. ⚠️ A THREE-WAY BLEND WAS ALWAYS THE WRONG SHAPE FOR THE VALLEY — it is not a place where three peoples meet, it is the place where EVERYONE'S craft has left a little behind. ✅ No dominant parent IS the character; the flat spread is the finding, not noise.
valley_craft._parentsBasis: ⚑ re-derived from 15 crafts carrying `learnedAt: valley_craft` after the R33 lineage assignment.

braids._ruling: ⛔ ERIK 2026-08-15: 'The crossroads needs to have PERFECT power sources. It's a MYSTERY OF THE WORLD that it exists — massive quests are here, with a mythical behind it. Likely a BRAID OF PRECURSOR AND VEIL that harmonizes all power sources, such as meta, nanite, etc.'

theCrossing.mechanic: ⛔ UNIVERSAL NEXUS — every power source reads ON-BAND at the Crossing, with no penalty for any.
theCrossing.cause: ⚠️ A STANDING BRAID OF PRECURSOR AND VEIL. Precursor wants density 0.90 and veil wants 0.10 — ⛔ THEY ARE EXACT MIRRORS, and `power_sources.json` already says so: 'the veil is the MIRROR of precursor, because thinning one strengthens the other.' A braid holding both in balance would cancel the density term entirely, which is what 'every axis crosses here at nothing' has always meant.
theCrossing.fiction: ⛔ NOBODY KNOWS WHY IT IS THERE. It is not a built thing anyone will admit to, and the braid holds without a wielder. ⚠️ THAT IS THE MYSTERY AND THE QUEST HOOK: something is sustaining a cross-pole braid at world scale, permanently, and the Crossing is the shadow it casts.
theCrossing.consequence: This is WHY braids cluster here and nowhere else — a braid needs two sources at once, and the Crossing is the only ground that gives both without cost. ⚠️ It also explains the Made Gate: a player built the 27th waygate HERE, and the 26 inherited ones are elsewhere.

notATradition.precursor: ⛔ A POWER SOURCE MISFILED AS A TRADITION. 6 abilities — Address-Sense, Latticespeak, Wake the Line, Unmake Seal, Hold the Aperture, Foreclose. No people owns them; anyone who learns to speak to the lattice has them. ⚠️ Should carry `tradition: null` with `powerSystem: precursor`.

_twoAxes:
⛔ SNG-443, ERIK'S RULING: 'Skills may be learned at PLACES — or in the wilds as a hunter — but they would be TIED BACK TO THEIR TRADITION ROOTS otherwise.'
⚠️ TWO SEPARATE AXES, AND I HAD COLLAPSED THEM:
   `tradition` — THE LINEAGE. Which people's craft this descends from. Permanent, and it is what the power source, the aesthetic and the wheel position all key off.
   `learnedAt` — THE ACCESS. Where a person can actually be taught it: a foothill, a school, a place, or the wilds.
⛔ A FOOTHILL IS A PLACE OF ACCESS, NOT A NEW ANCESTRY. Hardline teaches the Edge; it does not own it.
